The business model

How Snout Works

Wellness plans aren't new. They have been around for two decades, vendors have come and gone, PIMS systems have tried to build them, and nothing has really worked, because a wellness plan essentially means lending your customers money, interest free and credit check free, and hoping it works out in the end.

Run the old way, clinics are incented not to perform services because of breakage, codes and reconciliation get messy, and the program becomes a black box that makes more work than staff can handle. Best case, you are lending money and collecting it back over twelve months. The industry needed a product that works with clinic staff instead of creating work for them, one that removes the burden of collecting dollars, reconciling revenue, managing codes, and driving adoption without turning your front desk into a sales team.

Fundamentally, Snout pays clinics when they perform services. That simple, powerful change unlocks everything.
1 · Owner enrolls
2 minutes
At the clinic or from home. The owner pays Snout monthly.
2 · Pet visits
Normal codes
Built in the PIMS with your existing codes. Snout is simply the payment type.
3 · Revenue books
That instant
Closed invoice, recognized revenue, full doctor production. As if they paid by card.
4 · Cash arrives
~3 days
Paid weekly on Tuesdays for care performed, less one blended 3.7% fee.

What that unlocks

  • Staff focus on medicine, not reconciling codes.
  • Revenue books at service. Production and ProSal untouched.
  • Cash in days, not spread over twelve months.
  • Default and unlimited exam risk are Snout's.
  • Enrollment happens without your front desk selling.

A word on breakage

Some vendors will pitch breakage, the services members pay for and never use, as your upside. Treat that as a red flag. Breakage is not sustainable EBITDA. It erodes client satisfaction, drags renewal rates down point for point, and quietly turns your wellness program into the thing pet owners resent. Whatever you choose, do not build it into your unit economics.

This is exactly why every Snout plan includes unlimited office exams. Some breakage will always exist, and unlimited exams are our way of offsetting it and making sure pet owners get the value they are paying for. Because at the end of the day, if breakage exists, it means a pet owner overpaid.

Seven questions to ask every vendor, including us

How many member invoices have you processed, and who reviews the edge cases, software or people?

Over 700,000 member invoices and counting, processed automatically with a team of humans reviewing every edge case. Accuracy at the invoice line is the product, so we never let software guess alone.

Have you ever had a payment-data security incident? Ask for it in writing.

Never. Security and trust are the cornerstone of what we do, and we have never had an incident, backed by extensive testing, training, and a decade of experience. We are happy to put that in writing.

What is the largest rollout you have completed, not signed, and how long did it take?

Alliance Animal Health, where we are nearing 200 active clinics. The implementation ran in overlapping waves, and the lessons from it are folded into the four to five month playbook we would run for you.

Who carries the risk when a member defaults, and when a member uses more than they paid?

With Snout, we do, on both. You were paid when you performed the care, and if a member stops paying or uses their unlimited exams heavily, that is our cost, our outreach, and our problem. Ask every other vendor to point to the contract clause that says the same.

What happens when a clinic changes its codes or its prices mid-year?

We re-ingest them automatically. You are paid current prices as they change, and nobody rebuilds a plan, creates a code, or reconciles anything. Price protection is built in, not bolted on.

How much of your enrollment depends on discounting services?

For us, none. Discounting is the oldest trick in this category: it makes adoption look great while the cost falls straight to your bottom line. At a 20% EBITDA margin, a 10% discount cuts your profit in half. Snout plans are priced from each clinic's own fees with no markup and no discounts, and unlimited exams do the selling.

Name three groups running you at 50 or more clinics we can call this week.

Gladly, and we will arrange the calls this week. We are conscious of competitive dynamics in this process, so tell us who you want to speak with and we will make the introductions directly.

Steal this summary for your deck

Wellness plans are a proven lever for visit frequency and client retention, and the operating model matters as much as the software, because this is a change management exercise as much as a technology decision. Recommend a partner that pays clinics at time of service, carries the default and unlimited-exam risk, requires no new codes and no reconciliation, has completed multi-hundred-clinic rollouts, and does not bank on breakage, because breakage is deferred churn, not EBITDA. Pilot with one wave of 20 to 30 hand-raiser clinics, measure penetration, ACT lift, and visit frequency against baseline, and scale in overlapping waves through 2027.

Commercial & cash flow

Value to the Clinic

Some vendors will tell you their fee is lower, and that breakage, the services members pay for and never use, is EBITDA your clinics would otherwise keep. That is the old way of thinking about wellness plans, and it is how this industry burned clinics and pet owners the last time around. Weigh what each model actually delivers.

The real cost of pay over time models
  • You finance every plan for 12 months
  • Bad debt: consumer cards fail 4 to 5%
  • Staff hours reconciling codes
  • Mid-year price increases absorbed
  • No unlimited exams, or discounted DVM time
  • Discounts that come straight out of EBITDA
  • Breakage that comes back as churn at renewal
Snout, all in for one 3.7% fee
  • Cash at time of service, paid weekly
  • Unlimited exams, risk on Snout
  • Default risk on Snout
  • Zero collections, zero reconciliation
  • Marketing engine included
  • Clean rev rec, no mid-year price loss
  • Pharma rebates on top of your pricing
  • Execution proven at 200-clinic scale
The hidden cost of cash flow

With a pay over time wellness plan, the best case is that you get your money back twelve months later. But pets use most of their plan in the first month, and you pay the cost of goods behind those services right away. You incur the expense now and wait a year for the cash, and that costs you twice: the interest on the debt you carry, and the opportunity cost of capital you could be deploying into moves that lift your whole portfolio, like acquiring and improving clinics. Snout removes both. You are paid the week the care happens, and the lending sits on our balance sheet instead of yours.

The discount trick

Watch how many providers, especially the newest ones, lean on discounted services to make plans sell. A discount falls straight to your bottom line: at a 20% EBITDA margin, a 10% discount cuts your profit in half. Snout plans are priced from your own codes with no markup and no discounting, and unlimited exams do the selling instead.

The 3.7%, unpacked: we charge 5% on covered items and 2% on non-covered items, which blends to an average cost of 3.7% on our historical invoice volume. It is not in addition to card processing fees, it replaces them, and corporate groups typically pay 2 to 2.5% on cards today. A one-time $1,500 per location, scaling down with committed volume, is the only other cost. No per-plan fees, no minimums, no monthly fees.

Payments in practice

Invoices & Reconciliation

It starts with code mapping. We pull each clinic's invoice history and map every code with our own algorithm, refined across tens of millions of invoices and millions of mapped codes, with vet-experienced admins reviewing anything ambiguous. From then on, we already know what every line on every invoice is.

The clinic's raw codesPlan items

Every code a clinic uses, however it is named, maps to the plan item it belongs to. Several codes often roll up into one item.

What this replaces

Other providers make coverage depend on codes: use only their approved codes, create new ones just for the plan, or watch a service go uncovered at checkout. That is how wellness programs end up confusing front desk staff, upsetting pet owners, and burning hours in reconciliation. Code mapping is how we solved all of it, and it is the foundation everything else on this page sits on.

Clinics add codes, rename codes, and change prices all the time, and none of it is your problem. New and changed codes are flagged automatically, a human on our team reviews and maps them, and pricing updates flow through on their own. Nobody at the clinic maintains anything for Snout, ever.

Affordability & risk

Everyone Approved. Risk on Us.

We believe every pet should get access to care no matter what is in the owner's bank account. No credit checks, soft or hard. No age or breed restrictions. No waiting periods. Anyone 18 or older with a billing address can enroll. Snout carries the receivable, and if a client stops paying, we absorb the loss.

About those 99.8% capture-rate slides

Every vendor in this process rents the same smart retry technology. We use it too, and Snout brings millions more payment data points and a team of real humans on the phone to the problem. Here is the truth: at scale, consumer cards still fail 4 to 5% of the time. The difference is what happens next. With Snout it is our loss, our outreach, and our problem, at no fee to you. With everyone else, a missed payment is your receivable.

Getting a clinic live

Plan Design

Plan design is where a wellness program is won or lost, and it is the part of Snout we have spent the most time getting right. As a group you decide how many plans to offer and what goes in each. This page is how our plans work, and the few decisions that are yours to make.

It starts with unlimited office exams

Veterinary visits are down nationwide, and the reason is financial: the exam fee is a barrier to walking in the door. Remove it and pet owners stop hesitating. Our members average 5.7 visits per pet per year, more than double a typical non-member.

The only way to offer that without upsetting doctors is to keep them whole. Every exam a member uses is billed at the clinic's full rate and paid at the full rate, every time, and Snout underwrites the cost. Doctors are paid for their time, production is untouched, the barrier is gone, and every plan we sell includes it. That is the engine behind everything else on this page.

“Snout has empowered my clients to confidently say yes to preventive care. The unlimited free exams remove a significant financial barrier, so services that may once have been declined are now approved.”

Nicole Bradford, Practice Manager at Big Bend Animal Hospital
How Snout worksThe group sets the plan structure and guardrails once, and every hospital runs that set. Each clinic still keeps medical autonomy over which of its own codes qualify.

Plan items

Each plan is built from plan items, categories of care such as exams, vaccines, fecal screening, or bloodwork. Every item carries a dollar cap set during design, and any qualifying service the pet actually needs counts toward it. The clinic decides which services qualify, the veterinarian keeps full medical autonomy, and the owner sees one simple plan.

Add-ons

Base plans cover routine wellness. Add-ons let an owner cover the bigger, predictable expenses too, spread across the year. The group decides which to offer, and we recommend all three.

Spay / Neuter

The procedure plus pre-op bloodwork, priced by species, sex, and weight. You can limit it to puppies and kittens, or offer it at any age with a cap. Snout covers up to the priced amount, and the owner pays any difference for a higher-cost procedure.

~$30 to 60/mo

Dental

A routine stage 1 to 2 cleaning: prophy, anesthesia, IV catheter and fluids, full-mouth radiographs, and pre-op bloodwork. Extractions, nerve blocks, and take-home meds are not included. If worse disease is found, Snout covers up to the routine cleaning cost.

~$40 to 70/mo

Prevention

12 months of heartworm plus flea and tick prevention, using the clinic's chosen products, dispensed all at once or over time to match your protocol.

~$25 to 45/mo

Telemedicine

Airvet 24/7 teletriage is an optional clinic-wide election. Turned on, it adds roughly $5 per month to every plan and gives members around-the-clock access to a licensed vet between visits. We recommend it.

Who holds the pen

Structure is yours, set once at the group level and approved by you. Pricing is joint and specific to each clinic, because each one bills its own fees. Medical calls stay with the clinic inside your parameters, and anything non-standard is decided at the group level before it reaches a hospital. For a group that manages pricing centrally, the plan-draft call compresses to a short confirmation with the doctors.

Plan versions, and who keeps their plan

Members enroll into a specific version of a plan and keep it for their full term. Changes apply to new enrollees right away and to existing members at their next renewal, with each version tracked as its own cohort.

When the group is ready to make this concrete, the fastest step is a working session on one candidate clinic: real invoice data, a real plan draft, walked end to end.

No gotchas, and decisions made with data

When a plan says three vaccines, that means any three the provider deems necessary, and if four are on the invoice we cover the three most expensive. No core versus non-core, no booster exclusions. Standard-of-care debates get settled with each clinic's own invoice history, and every design choice is approved by you before launch.

How we work with groups

Rollout, in Waves

We recommend overlapping waves of 20 to 30 clinics. A wave takes four to five weeks end to end, and all 200 clinics take four to five months. We have implemented 200 clinics for another corporate before, so this is not our first time.

A new wave of 20 to 30 hospitals starts every two to three weeks, with the next wave kicking off once the prior wave clears its plan drafts. We lock the exact cadence with your team up front against a shared capacity plan, so several waves overlap, the group moves quickly, and no single hospital is rushed.

Why waves

Waves beat both a big bang launch and going one clinic at a time:

  • Clinics launch better together. Teams work through the same things at the same moment.
  • Faster feedback loops. Each wave teaches the next one.
  • Everyone stays organized. A predictable cadence with clear dates, and no one underwater.
  • Real attention per hospital. A focused launch, not one of hundreds on the same day.

How this model works, in plain language

It takes your assumptions from above and layers in the average lift we see from Snout members: a 44% increase in ACT and a 72% increase in visit frequency, our two published medians.

We combine those with your enrollment pace, the wave schedule, the renewal rate, the inflation assumption, and your margins. Members enroll monthly from each clinic's go-live, each cohort shifts to member behavior, renews annually, and the whole network compounds from the January 1, 2027 launch.

Incremental revenue is the with-Snout network minus the without-Snout network. Incremental EBITDA applies your contribution margin on incremental services. Penetration is active members divided by active patients across the network. Every number here traces to the downloadable Excel model and the scenario CSV.

The RFP

Your Questions, Answered

Every question from your RFP, in your categories. The same answers appear in the completed questionnaire that accompanies this page.

ezyVet integration

Describe your ezyVet integration. Is enrollment, charge capture, and redemption automatic?

A read-only data connection powers everything: plan creation from your own codes and pricing, an enrollment flow that recognizes your clients and their pets, and fully automatic invoice processing with your normal codes. More than 100 clinics run Snout on ezyVet today, and reference clinics are available on request.

How are plan-included line items zeroed out at invoice? What reconciliation is required at month-end?

You keep your normal codes and pricing, and there is never manual reconciliation, at service or at month end. Staff include everything on the invoice, covered or not, and Snout processes it automatically. We have processed tens of millions of invoices over a decade, and getting this exactly right is the foundation the software is built on.

Ease of admin

Walk through the front-desk enrollment flow. Average time? What training is required?

There is no front desk flow to learn, because enrollment is 100% online, mobile optimized, and takes about 60 seconds. Each clinic gets a dedicated URL connected to its PIMS, owners are invited by personalized email and SMS, materials, and QR codes, and they enroll themselves. Staff can help if they want to, and never have to.

How are failed payments handled, and who does the outreach?

They are our problem, not yours. You were paid when you performed the care, and Snout takes the default risk. We run smart retries, offer second payment methods, and put a dedicated human team on helping owners get current. And because every plan includes unlimited exams, at roughly $60 a month against what a single exam typically costs, members are always incented to stay current. Expect anyone's consumer cards to fail 4 to 5%, whatever the slide says.

Can we manage all locations' plans through a single portal and make changes centrally?

Yes. Every group gets a dedicated corporate portal: set plan parameters, invite stakeholders from the operations level to the executive level, approve pricing before a clinic ever sees it, watch every clinic's onboarding stage, nudge stalls, and join any training. The demo logins included with this proposal show it directly.

What is the ability to control access and permissions by role or user?

Corporate leadership sees the whole organization, and regional or operations directors can be scoped to exactly their clinics across pricing, onboarding, and enrollment visibility.

Penetration

Provide adoption and penetration rates, and what drives them.

Across our book, the median clinic sells about 38 new plans per month and the average is 54, with slower clinics around 17 and top performers reaching about 90. Penetration compounds from that pace: at the average pace a clinic crosses roughly 10% of its active patients in its first year and keeps climbing as renewals stack, and the Build Your Business Case page in this proposal models exactly that against your own patient counts. On the drivers: this is a change management exercise, and the biggest lever is pet owners arriving already sold. Pre-appointment email and SMS 7 days and 2 days before wellness visits lift enrollments about 28%. Add digital front doors, printed materials we design and pay for, staff trained to talk compliance rather than sell, short-term team incentives we fund with your approval, and a named CSM with at least nine years of in-clinic experience.

Provide case studies for penetration, per-pet spend, visit frequency, and revenue lift.

Provided separately, and summarized on the ROI & Case Studies page of this proposal.

What are average pre-term cancellation and breakage rates?

We take a lifetime value lens: every point of breakage costs a point of renewals, so we design to drive usage rather than keep it. Lifecycle outreach triggers when a pet is behind on usage, clinics get unused benefit reports, and plan items are deliberately broad, so three vaccines means any three the provider deems necessary. Specific rates are best discussed live, alongside the design choices that drive them.

What marketing collateral do you provide, and is it co-brandable across our legacy brands?

The full stack, included at no cost: pre-appointment invitations, lifecycle and winback campaigns, printed materials we design, pay for, and deliver, website and social assets, and QR codes. Everything is branded per clinic, so each AmeriVet legacy brand keeps its identity.

Plan design

Can we run Good/Better/Best tiers and per-pet dynamic add-ons, standardized across 200 sites with local pricing?

Yes to both, and you can A/B test them across clinics. Standardize the structure and tiers centrally, keep medical autonomy at the clinic inside your parameters, and Snout prices everything from each clinic's own codes and does all the live work, with corporate approval before anything ships.

How easily can each individual clinic edit the bundles?

Clinics choose freely from a medical perspective within the parameters you set. The structure is yours, the medicine is theirs, and we inform both with each clinic's own historical invoice data.

Affordability

Is there a credit check? Who carries the receivable, and who absorbs the loss?

No credit checks, soft or hard. No age or breed restrictions, no waiting periods. Anyone 18 or older with a billing address can enroll. Snout carries the receivable and absorbs the loss if a client stops paying. You get paid for the services you perform.

Enterprise & reporting

Describe role-based access and the reporting available to corporate leadership.

Clinic-level reports go to clinics and corporate roll-ups come to you, by email, SFTP, or API. The core reports are enrollments, invoices processed, usage, and payouts. The ROI layer goes deeper: ACT versus historical baseline, compliance rates across wellness items before and after, and enrollment, cancellation, and renewal trends across clinics, regions, and the book.

Can reporting be customized, for example for operations directors who each manage 10 to 15 clinics?

Yes. Slice by operations director, geography, pricing tier, or onboarding wave, real time and automated. We set it up with you during onboarding and change it whenever you like.

What are the API capabilities for key operational KPIs?

Yes. We typically start with email or file delivery for the first few weeks while your BI team confirms exactly which fields it wants, then stand up the API. Not a problem at all.

How do you support GAAP revenue recognition and feeds to our BI team?

Revenue is recognized when care is performed, booked in your PIMS with your normal codes and pricing, that instant. Nothing about rev rec, production, or ProSal changes, and your existing BI reporting keeps working because we never alter the PIMS data.

Enterprise deployment

Largest multi-site rollout to date, timeline, and required client headcount?

We work with 12 enterprise groups today, deeply embedded, and we have implemented 200 clinics for a single corporate before, in six to seven months, with the lessons folded into the four to five month path we would run now. Clinics give three 30-minute meetings. Corporate gives one point person and a weekly check-in. References gladly, and we are conscious of competitive dynamics, so tell us who you want to talk to.

Commercial & cash flow

Full pricing: setup, fees, processing, minimums, and term commitments.

One blended 3.7% per transaction we process, which includes payment processing and the cost of capital of paying you up front. No per-site or per-plan fees, no minimums, no monthly or collections fees. A one-time $1,500 implementation fee per location, scaling down with committed volume and flexible, covers marketing materials, staff incentives, integration maintenance, and member support.

When is the practice paid for services rendered under a plan?

When you perform them. We batch payments weekly on Tuesdays, so at most a seven day lag and about three days on average from service to cash.

Implementation & support

Typical time-to-launch for a single site and a 20-site wave? What do we resource internally?

A wave of 20 to 30 clinics takes four to five weeks end to end, waves overlap, and 200 clinics is a four to five month program. Your side names an owner, joins a weekly check-in, and makes two decisions with us: plan structure, which is a medical conversation, and one marketing planning call so materials match your brand. We do the heavy lifting.

What post-launch support is included?

No additional cost. Dedicated onboarding, clinic success, and member support teams, a named CSM per group, a member app for self-service, and call, text, and email support answered by real humans, so questions never land on your front desk.

Compliance

How does your platform handle multi-state wellness plan regulation?

Out of the box. Disclosure, trial, cancellation, and refund mechanics for service-contract states are embedded in our membership and practice agreements, and we are compliant in all states, period.

Viability

Share ownership, funding, customer growth, and product roadmap, especially ezyVet and IDEXX work.

We raised $110 million in January: institutional venture equity plus a $100 million revolving debt facility that funds paying clinics up front. Fifty US-based full-time team members, go-to-market together in our Michigan office, and a US W-2 engineering team. We are independent, intend to remain independent, and are not in acquisition or joint venture discussions with any consolidator. On ezyVet and IDEXX: our plans auto-renew and carry bloodwork in every adult plan, which drives exactly the recurring lab compliance IDEXX cares about, and we are close with their senior leadership.

Data & exit

If we leave, what happens to active members and their data?

Your data and your relationships are yours, in writing, in the practice agreement. Everything is portable today, and we support handoff and migration with the same white glove treatment. Strict security and deletion protocols throughout.
